investments.name: Public Provident Fund (PPF)
investments.description: The Public Provident Fund (PPF) is a long-term government-backed small savings scheme in India, aimed at providing retirement security and tax-efficient wealth creation.
investments.plainLanguageSummary: PPF is a safe, long-term savings scheme where you can invest small amounts annually to build a retirement corpus, enjoy tax-free interest, and claim tax deductions on your deposits.
investments.maturityRules: Matures after 15 years, extendable in blocks of 5 years.
investments.withdrawalRules: Partial withdrawal allowed from 7th financial year onwards.
investments.prematureWithdrawalRules: Not allowed, except in cases of death of the account holder.
investments.taxBenefits: Deduction under Section 80C up to ₹1.5 Lakh per annum.
investments.taxation: EEE (Exempt-Exempt-Exempt): Deposits, Interest, and Maturity amount are all tax-exempt.
investments.applicationMethod: Open an account at any authorized bank or post office branch.
investments.documentsRequired: Identity Proof (Aadhaar/PAN), Address Proof, Passport size photos.

faqItems.question: What is the lock-in period?
faqItems.answer: The lock-in period is 15 years, with partial withdrawal allowed after the 7th year.

faqItems.question: Is PPF tax-free?
faqItems.answer: Yes, PPF follows the EEE (Exempt-Exempt-Exempt) taxation regime.

faqItems.question: Can I extend PPF?
faqItems.answer: Yes, accounts can be extended in blocks of 5 years after maturity.

faqItems.question: What if I miss a deposit?
faqItems.answer: The account becomes inactive. It can be revived by paying a small penalty.

faqItems.question: Can I take a loan?
faqItems.answer: Yes, loans are available between the 3rd and 6th financial year.

investments.name: National Pension System (NPS)
investments.description: The National Pension System (NPS) is a voluntary, long-term retirement savings scheme regulated by the PFRDA, offering market-linked returns.
investments.plainLanguageSummary: NPS helps you build a retirement corpus through market-linked investments. It offers tax efficiency, flexibility in asset allocation, and is portable across locations and jobs.
investments.maturityRules: Matures at age 60, with options for deferment up to age 75.
investments.withdrawalRules: Partial withdrawal (up to 25%) allowed for specific purposes after 3 years.
investments.prematureWithdrawalRules: Full withdrawal allowed only under specific conditions; otherwise 80% of corpus must be annuitized.
investments.taxBenefits: Deduction under 80C, plus an exclusive deduction of ₹50,000 under 80CCD(1B).
investments.taxation: EET: Contributions and interest are exempt, but annuity and lump-sum withdrawal are taxable as per slab.
investments.riskInformation: Moderate to High (Subject to market risks)
investments.applicationMethod: Register online via eNPS or visit a Point of Presence (PoP) bank.
investments.documentsRequired: Identity Proof (PAN), Address Proof, Bank account details.

faqItems.question: Is NPS return guaranteed?
faqItems.answer: No, returns depend on the market performance of chosen investment funds.

faqItems.question: Can I choose my asset mix?
faqItems.answer: Yes, you can choose between Active Choice (auto-rebalancing or self) and Auto Choice.

faqItems.question: What is Tier 1 vs Tier 2?
faqItems.answer: Tier 1 is for retirement (restricted); Tier 2 is a flexible, withdrawable account.

faqItems.question: Can I exit before 60?
faqItems.answer: Yes, but strict withdrawal rules apply on how the corpus is handled.

faqItems.question: How is the annuity provided?
faqItems.answer: Upon maturity, a portion must be used to purchase an annuity from a PFRDA-registered service provider.

faqItems.question: Can I continue after 60?
faqItems.answer: Yes, NPS can be extended up to the age of 75.

investments.name: Unified Pension Scheme (UPS)
investments.description: The Unified Pension Scheme (UPS) provides an assured pension for central government employees, combining features of defined-benefit and defined-contribution models.
investments.plainLanguageSummary: UPS offers a guaranteed pension of 50% of the last 12 months average basic pay for employees with 25+ years of service, with pro-rated benefits for shorter service, and family pension provisions.
keyBenefits: Assured pension of 50% of average basic pay
investments.maturityRules: Matures at age 60, with minimum 10 years of service.
investments.prematureWithdrawalRules: Not applicable, as it is a retirement pension scheme.
investments.taxation: As per existing tax laws for pension schemes.

faqItems.question: Who is eligible for UPS?
faqItems.answer: Central government employees who were in service as of March 31, 2025, or new recruits joining on or after April 1, 2025.

faqItems.question: Is the pension guaranteed?
faqItems.answer: Yes, 50% of the average basic pay of the last 12 months for 25 years of service.

faqItems.question: What is the minimum pension?
faqItems.answer: ₹10,000 per month for at least 10 years of service.

faqItems.question: Does it cover family?
faqItems.answer: Yes, spouse receives 60% of the assured pension.

faqItems.question: Is it optional?
faqItems.answer: Yes, it is an option within the existing NPS framework.

investments.name: National Savings Certificate (NSC)
investments.description: The National Savings Certificate (NSC) is a fixed-income investment scheme offered by the government, providing safety and tax benefits.
investments.plainLanguageSummary: NSC is a secure, 5-year savings plan with a fixed interest rate. It is ideal for conservative investors looking for guaranteed returns and tax savings.
keyBenefits: Fixed interest rate for the tenure
investments.prematureWithdrawalRules: Not allowed, except in cases of death of account holder or court order.
investments.taxBenefits: Deduction under Section 80C up to ₹1.5 Lakh per annum.
investments.taxation: Taxable: Interest earned is taxable as per individual slab, but qualifies for 80C deduction when reinvested.
investments.applicationMethod: Apply at any post office branch.

faqItems.question: Is NSC tax-free?
faqItems.answer: No, interest is taxable, but the invested amount qualifies for 80C deduction.

faqItems.question: Can I withdraw NSC early?
faqItems.answer: No, premature withdrawal is restricted.

faqItems.question: Is interest compounded?
faqItems.answer: Yes, interest is compounded annually and paid at maturity.

faqItems.question: Can I invest jointly?
faqItems.answer: Yes, a joint account is allowed.

faqItems.question: Are returns guaranteed?
faqItems.answer: Yes, the interest rate is fixed at the time of purchase for the entire tenure.

faqItems.question: Can minors invest?
faqItems.answer: Yes, minors can be account holders.

investments.name: Kisan Vikas Patra (KVP)
investments.description: Kisan Vikas Patra (KVP) is a long-term fixed-income savings scheme where the invested amount doubles over a specific period.
investments.plainLanguageSummary: KVP is a simple scheme designed to double your investment over a fixed period. It is safe, government-backed, and provides guaranteed returns.
investments.taxation: Taxable: Interest is fully taxable as per income slab.
investments.applicationMethod: Open at any post office branch.

faqItems.question: When does money double?
faqItems.answer: The investment doubles in 115 months.

faqItems.question: Is it tax-free?
faqItems.answer: No, interest is fully taxable.

faqItems.question: Can I withdraw early?
faqItems.answer: Yes, after a lock-in period of 2.5 years.

faqItems.question: Is joint account allowed?
faqItems.answer: Yes.

faqItems.question: Can minors open it?
faqItems.answer: Yes, minors can be account holders.

faqItems.question: Are returns fixed?
faqItems.answer: Yes, guaranteed as per the scheme terms.

investments.name: Senior Citizen Savings Scheme (SCSS)
investments.description: The Senior Citizen Savings Scheme (SCSS) is a government-backed investment product specifically for individuals aged 60 and above, offering regular interest income.
investments.plainLanguageSummary: SCSS is a highly safe, quarterly-interest-paying scheme perfect for senior citizens to generate steady income with tax-saving benefits.
investments.taxBenefits: Deduction under Section 80C up to ₹1.5 Lakh per annum.
investments.taxation: Taxable: Interest is taxable as per income slab.
investments.applicationMethod: Open at Post Office or authorized bank.
investments.documentsRequired: Age proof, Identity proof, Address proof.

faqItems.question: Who can open SCSS?
faqItems.answer: Individuals aged 60+.

faqItems.question: How often is interest paid?
faqItems.answer: Interest is paid quarterly.

faqItems.question: Can I extend it?
faqItems.answer: Yes, after 5 years, it can be extended for 3 more years.

faqItems.question: Is interest tax-free?
faqItems.answer: No, it is taxable.

faqItems.question: What is the limit?
faqItems.answer: Maximum ₹30 Lakh per individual.

faqItems.question: Can I close it early?
faqItems.answer: Yes, with a penalty based on time of closure.

investments.name: Sukanya Samriddhi Account (SSA)
investments.description: The Sukanya Samriddhi Account (SSA) is a government-backed small savings scheme designed for the financial welfare of a girl child.
investments.plainLanguageSummary: SSA is a secure investment for the girl child, offering high tax-free interest and long-term security to fund education or marriage expenses.
keyBenefits: Higher interest rate compared to most savings schemes
investments.maturityRules: 21 years from account opening or upon marriage after 18.
investments.withdrawalRules: Partial withdrawal (up to 50%) for education allowed after age 18.
investments.taxBenefits: Deduction under Section 80C up to ₹1.5 Lakh per annum.
investments.taxation: EEE (Exempt-Exempt-Exempt): Deposits, Interest, and Maturity amount are all tax-exempt.
investments.nominationRules: Not applicable (account is in the name of the child).
investments.applicationMethod: Open at Post Office or authorized bank.
investments.documentsRequired: Birth Certificate of girl child, Parent/Guardian ID.

faqItems.question: Who is eligible?
faqItems.answer: Girl child below 10 years of age.

faqItems.question: When does it mature?
faqItems.answer: 21 years from account opening.

faqItems.question: Can I withdraw for education?
faqItems.answer: Yes, up to 50% for higher education after age 18.

faqItems.question: Is interest taxable?
faqItems.answer: No, interest earned is tax-exempt.

faqItems.question: What if I miss a deposit?
faqItems.answer: Account can be revived by paying penalty.

faqItems.question: How many accounts?
faqItems.answer: Maximum two accounts per family (three in case of twins/triplets).

investments.name: Post Office Recurring Deposit (PORD)
investments.description: Post Office Recurring Deposit (PORD) is a savings scheme allowing monthly investments for a period of 5 years with fixed interest.
investments.plainLanguageSummary: PORD is a disciplined savings scheme where you deposit a fixed amount every month for 5 years to build a lump sum with guaranteed interest.
investments.taxation: Taxable: Interest earned is taxable as per individual income slab.

faqItems.question: What is the tenure?
faqItems.answer: Fixed at 5 years.

faqItems.question: How is interest calculated?
faqItems.answer: Compounded quarterly at the applicable rate.

faqItems.answer: Minimum is ₹100, can be increased in multiples of ₹10.

faqItems.question: What if I miss a monthly deposit?
faqItems.answer: A penalty is charged; if multiple missed, the account may be discontinued.

faqItems.question: Can I withdraw early?
faqItems.answer: Yes, premature closure is allowed after 3 years.

faqItems.question: Can I open a joint account?
faqItems.answer: Yes.

schemes.detailedDescription: PM Schools for Rising India (PM SHRI) is a centrally sponsored scheme aimed at developing more than 14,500 schools across India into model schools, incorporating the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 features to provide high-quality education in an equitable and inclusive environment.
schemes.eligibility: Selected government schools based on performance and potential.
schemes.benefits: Infrastructure upgrade, technological integration, and high-quality learning resources.
schemes.applicationProcess: Apply through MoE portal (for participating schools).
schemes.documentsRequired: School data, performance reports.

faqItems.question: What is PM SHRI?
faqItems.answer: Centrally sponsored scheme for developing model schools.

faqItems.question: What is the goal?
faqItems.answer: To provide high-quality education in an inclusive environment based on NEP 2020.

faqItems.question: Who benefits?
faqItems.answer: Students and the school community.

faqItems.question: Are all schools included?
faqItems.answer: Selected schools are upgraded to model standards.

faqItems.question: What are the features?
faqItems.answer: Infrastructure upgrade, technology, and quality learning resources.

faqItems.question: How is it implemented?
faqItems.answer: In partnership with states and UTs.

schemes.shortDescription: A comprehensive policy framework for India's logistics sector.
schemes.detailedDescription: The National Logistics Policy (NLP) provides an overarching, interdisciplinary, cross-sectoral, and comprehensive policy framework for India's logistics sector. It complements the PM GatiShakti National Master Plan and aims to improve logistics efficiency, reduce costs, and enhance the competitiveness of Indian businesses through multimodal connectivity, digital integration, and infrastructure development.
schemes.targetBeneficiary: Logistics service providers, businesses, manufacturers, and traders.
schemes.eligibility: General policy framework applicable to the logistics and supply chain ecosystem.
schemes.benefits: Enhanced logistics efficiency, reduced costs, and improved multimodal connectivity.
keyBenefits: Digitalisation and integration of logistics services
schemes.applicationProcess: Implemented through institutional frameworks and cross-sectoral coordination.
schemes.documentsRequired: N/A.

faqItems.question: What is the National Logistics Policy?
faqItems.answer: An overarching policy framework to improve India's logistics efficiency.

faqItems.question: What is its objective?
faqItems.answer: To reduce logistics costs and enhance business competitiveness.

faqItems.question: How does it relate to PM GatiShakti?
faqItems.answer: It complements the PM GatiShakti National Master Plan.

faqItems.question: Who benefits?
faqItems.answer: Logistics service providers, businesses, and traders.

faqItems.question: Does it offer direct subsidies?
faqItems.answer: No, it is a policy framework focused on systemic improvements.

faqItems.question: What is the implementation focus?
faqItems.answer: Multimodal connectivity, digital integration, and infrastructure development.

schemes.seoTitle: National Logistics Policy (NLP): Comprehensive Framework 2026

schemes.shortDescription: National mission to position India as a global leader in technical textiles.
schemes.detailedDescription: The NTTM focuses on research, development, promotion, and application of technical textiles to boost India’s position as a global leader in this specialized sector, including fibers for healthcare, infra, and geo-technical uses.

schemes.eligibility: Manufacturing units and research organizations working in the field of technical textiles.
schemes.benefits: Financial support for R&D, market development, and manufacturing.

faqItems.answer: Textiles engineered for specific functional applications.

faqItems.question: What is the goal of NTTM?
faqItems.answer: To make India a global leader in technical textiles.

faqItems.question: Who can benefit?
faqItems.answer: Manufacturers and R&D entities.
